title: There is no single substrate for memory; all components can serve as scratchpads

fields.label: Label
fields.value: There is no single substrate for memory; all components can serve as scratchpads

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Levin hypothesizes that there is no single substrate for memory: every component of a living system can use everything in its environment, including the high-dimensional reservoir of subcellular structure, as an interpretable scratchpad, rather than engrams residing only in synapses.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 6. What It Means, and What Next: A Research Program for Further Development

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: My current hypothesis, driven by the above multi-scale perspective [218], is that there is no single substrate for memory49.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue”, Entropy (Basel, Switzerland) (2024), doi:10.3390/e26060481; section “6. What It Means, and What Next: A Research Program for Further Development”. Scope: Nervous systems and non-neural tissues

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-memory-14: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.40

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Distributed memory has measurable restricted versions and abundant neural and molecular data. The claim's universal scope and scratchpad metaphor exceed existing perturbation coverage and make decisive discrimination difficult.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For multiple learning paradigms, test whether memory retrieval survives disruption of candidate synaptic, epigenetic, intracellular and peripheral stores and whether each component's state predicts later recall beyond synaptic state. Evidence for several independently necessary or sufficient stores supports a distributed-substrate version.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Decoding information from a component does not prove it stores memory.

Datasets rarely pair causal perturbations across substrate classes.

The universal phrase every component is effectively unfalsifiable.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Published work on intrinsic excitability, epigenetic persistence, and behavior after loss of brain tissue can challenge the rival that engrams reside only in synapses. That is a partial test, and the studies would have to be compiled by hand. The positive claim that there is no privileged substrate and that every component can be used as a scratchpad is stronger than those cases and is not covered by any existing dataset.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: After a defined training stimulus, test whether the changed response persists when synaptic transmission, intrinsic excitability, or non-neural cell state is disrupted one at a time. Persistence after synaptic disruption would refute a synapse-only substrate; showing that some component classes cannot store the change would refute the claim that every component can serve as a scratchpad.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Training protocols and readouts are not comparable across synapses, epigenomes, and tissues.

A universal quantifier over every component cannot be confirmed by a finite set of substrates.

Evidence for non-synaptic and non-neural memory is scattered across literatures and is not one dataset.
